NDT training in the Rockies and Plains: how it works

Short answer: Across the Rockies and Plains, NDT theory is studied online through the Atlantis portal at your own pace, with an ASNT NDT Level III to answer questions, and the hands-on training and practical examination take place at the employer's shop, yard or field base under a written practice built on ASNT SNT-TC-1A. Your employer certifies you, not the course. Atlantis NDT has no classroom in the Rockies and Plains; its offices are in Houston, Texas and Hyderabad, India.

Distance shapes everything in this region. A technician in Williston, Casper or Billings can be hours from the nearest NDT school, and field crews spend weeks on the road between basins, digs and refinery turnarounds. Online theory that opens the moment you enrol, in any month, removes the travel from the classroom part; the practical then happens where the employer keeps its equipment. The published US course fees on this page cover Level I and Level II in UT, RT, MT, PT and VT, and course detail for the whole country sits on NDT training in the USA.

Where NDT technicians work across the Rockies and Plains

Denver and the DJ Basin. Production in the Denver-Julesburg Basin, much of it in Weld County north of the city, keeps gathering lines, compressor stations and processing plants busy with weld and corrosion examination. Suncor's refinery in Commerce City, Colorado's single refinery, adds turnaround work, and space and defense manufacturing along the Front Range brings precision NDT for aerospace customers. See NDT training in Denver, Colorado Springs and Colorado.

The Bakken and the Williston Basin. North Dakota's oil country runs on well sites, gathering systems, gas processing plants and the pipelines that carry crude and natural gas liquids out of the basin. Williston is the service hub, and its NDT work follows the drilling and construction cycle: busy when pipe goes in the ground, quieter when prices fall. See North Dakota.

Billings and the Montana refineries. Three refineries in and around Billings process crude from Canada and the Rockies, and each runs periodic turnarounds that pull in contract inspection crews from across the region. Between turnarounds, the work is thickness monitoring, piping inspection and tank examination. See Montana.

Wyoming. Oil and gas production, gas processing plants and the state's refineries sit far apart, and Casper serves as a base for crews covering them. Wind farms on the plains add tower and flange weld examination. See Wyoming.

Salt Lake City and northern Utah. A cluster of refineries on the north side of Salt Lake City supplies fuel across the Intermountain West, Rio Tinto Kennecott's Bingham Canyon mine and smelter run heavy equipment and process plant to the west, and the Ogden Air Logistics Complex at Hill Air Force Base maintains military aircraft. That mix gives Utah refinery, mining and aviation NDT within a short drive. See Ogden and Utah.

Wichita and Kansas. Wichita builds aircraft: Textron Aviation makes Cessna and Beechcraft airplanes, and the large fuselage plant that was Spirit AeroSystems became part of Boeing when Boeing completed the acquisition in December 2025. Aerospace NDT there is penetrant, magnetic particle, ultrasonic and eddy current work to the customer's specifications, with personnel certified under the employer's written practice, built on SNT-TC-1A and aligned with the prime's flow-down and Nadcap AC7114. Refineries elsewhere in the state add plant work. See Kansas.

Tulsa, Oklahoma City and Cushing. Tulsa combines refining with a long-established process-equipment fabrication industry building heat exchangers, pressure vessels and air coolers, and American Airlines runs a large maintenance base there. Oklahoma City is home to the Oklahoma City Air Logistics Complex at Tinker Air Force Base, which overhauls military aircraft and engines. Between the two cities, Cushing's tank farms hold crude at the delivery point for the benchmark WTI futures contract, so tank inspection to API 653 is steady work. See Oklahoma.

Idaho Falls. Idaho National Laboratory, the Department of Energy's nuclear research site west of Idaho Falls, brings examination work under DOE quality-assurance requirements, a different documentation culture from oilfield practice.

Which NDT methods and levels Rockies and Plains employers ask for

Field contractors want Level II technicians who can run a job alone and report it correctly, because the supervising Level III is often in another state. Level I trainees work alongside them and build hours. The common pairings look like this.

SectorMethods employers wantCodes and documents that govern acceptance
Pipeline construction and integrity digsVT, RT, UT, MTAPI 1104, 49 CFR Parts 192 and 195, operator procedures
Gas processing and refiningUT thickness, VT, PT, MT, RT; PAUT on weldsAPI 510, API 570, ASME B31.3, ASME Section V
Tank farms (Cushing, terminals)UT, VT, MT, MFL floor scanningAPI 653, owner specifications
Process-equipment fabrication (Tulsa, Wichita)VT, MT, PT, UT, RTASME Section VIII, ASME B31.3, AWS D1.1
Aircraft manufacture (Wichita)PT, MT, UT, ET, VTCustomer specifications, ASTM E1417, ASTM E1444, Nadcap AC7114
Airline and military depot maintenanceET, UT, PT, MT, VTManufacturer maintenance manuals, FAA-accepted programmes, Air Force technical orders
Mining and windUT, MT, VTAWS D1.1, owner and manufacturer specifications

In oil and gas country, VT plus RT or UT gets a newcomer onto pipeline spreads, and UT thickness work leads into plant and tank inspection; the ultrasonic testing training page lays out that path. Aviation employers in Wichita, Tulsa and Oklahoma City lean on PT, ET and UT. The Level 1 and Level 2 training pages show what each level allows a technician to do alone.

How certification works for mobile crews in the Rockies and Plains

None of the region's states issues an NDT license by method, so a certification issued by your employer covers you wherever that employer sends you. A UT Level II certified by a Denver contractor works a dig in North Dakota or a turnaround in Billings on the same certificate, because SNT-TC-1A certification follows the company's written practice, not the state line. That is what makes field work across the region possible.

It stops at the company door, though. Change employers and the new one recertifies you under its own written practice, typically with new specific and practical examinations and a vision check, using your documented training and hours as the basis. Field technicians often lose track of logged hours on the road; keep a running, signed record of every job, method and supervising technician.

For field work the written practice itself has to be built for distance: it should state who may administer examinations at a field base, how the Level III reviews results remotely and how records reach the company file. Employers whose document was written for a single shop can bring it up to date through written practice development. ASNT central certification is the alternative that belongs to the technician; at Level III, the ASNT certificate is the usual examination basis for the employer's Level III certification, and Atlantis prepares candidates through ASNT Level III training. Pipeline operators add operator qualification under 49 CFR Parts 192 and 195, aviation depots and airlines run their own qualification on top, and none of those replaces method certification. Check your own position with the SNT-TC-1A eligibility checker.

Radiography licensing across the Rockies and Plains states

An RT course gives you technique and interpretation; it does not license you to use a radioactive source. That licensing depends on the state. Colorado, Utah, North Dakota, Kansas and Oklahoma are NRC Agreement States, so their own agencies license industrial radiography: the Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment, Utah's Division of Waste Management and Radiation Control, the North Dakota Department of Environmental Quality, the Kansas Department of Health and Environment and the Oklahoma Department of Environmental Quality. Montana is not an Agreement State, so radiography licences there come from the NRC, through its Region IV office.

Two details matter for crews that cross the map. A company licensed in one state applies for reciprocity before radiographing in the next. And on some federal and tribal land, the NRC keeps jurisdiction even inside an Agreement State, which can apply to pipeline and oilfield work on reservations, so confirm who regulates the site before a crew mobilizes. Under 10 CFR Part 34 and the matching state rules, radiographers complete radiation-safety training and a radiographer certification examination, and assistants work under a radiographer's personal supervision. Atlantis does not perform radiography in the United States; our radiographic testing training prepares you for the employer's RT examinations.

Choosing an NDT training provider in the Rockies and Plains

Schools with labs cluster in the larger metros such as Denver, Salt Lake City, Tulsa and Oklahoma City, and some community colleges teach NDT or welding inspection. For someone in a basin town, the choice usually comes down to one question: can you afford weeks away from home and work?

  • Relocating to a school. Full-time programmes give hands-on time from the start and suit someone with no NDT employer, but they mean travel, lodging and lost earnings.
  • Starting as a helper. Field contractors take on helpers and arrange formal training as experience builds. Ask how the formal hours will be delivered and documented before you sign on.
  • Online theory with the practical at your employer. The Atlantis route: theory at your own pace with Level III support, simulator practice, then hands-on training and examination at the employer's base. It suits technicians already employed, and companies that cannot spare crews mid-season.

Whichever you pick, confirm that the hours will satisfy your employer's written practice, find out who will examine your practical and on what, and make sure you leave with records a future employer will accept. Any provider that promises to certify you is describing something only an employer can do under SNT-TC-1A. The NDT training overview and the NDT training FAQ cover how Atlantis courses work.

Training a crew spread across basins and plants

A contractor running crews in the DJ Basin, the Bakken and a Billings turnaround at the same time cannot pull everyone into one room. Theory online solves the classroom half: technicians work through it in motels and camp housing between shifts, on the same material and to the same written practice.

The hands-on half comes to a place you choose, usually your shop or main yard. The ASNT NDT Level III behind Atlantis courses holds UT, RT, MT, PT and VT and brings 11+ years of field work; training and examinations run on your instruments, procedures and representative samples, so a technician is examined on the work the crew actually does. Each person's file ends up with training hours, experience, examination results and vision records organized to your written practice, which is what an operator's auditor asks to see. Send your bases, methods and head-count through the training enquiry form. We reply within one business day.

Practise before your practical examination

Field candidates rarely have a spare instrument and a stack of flawed samples at home. Practical NDT fills that gap with a 3D simulator that runs in a browser, in VR, or on a PC that can work offline once downloaded, which helps on a rig-site connection. It walks you through a twelve-step procedure and the evaluator credits only what you record. Try the UT simulator for thickness and weld work, the radiography simulator for pipeline RT technique, and the storage-tank workplace for terminal jobs. Practice in the simulator prepares you; the supervised hours, hands-on practical and employer certification still have to be completed in person.

For the written side, use the free Level II practice tests, method by method.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in the Rockies and Plains

How long does NDT training take in the Rockies and Plains?

The formal hours are set per method and level by the employer's written practice, following SNT-TC-1A, and the theory moves at your own pace. Experience hours are the longer part, especially when field work is seasonal. The training requirements matrix shows the recommended hours.

Can I do NDT training online from North Dakota, Montana or Wyoming?

Yes, the theory runs online wherever you are. The hands-on training and practical examination take place in person at your employer's facility. See NDT training online.

Is there an NDT school near me in Denver, Tulsa or Salt Lake City?

Atlantis does not run one there or anywhere else. The city pages linked above describe each local market, and for companies the training is delivered at their own facility.

Which NDT method should I start with for oilfield work?

VT with RT or UT for pipeline construction, and UT for plant and tank inspection. MT and PT round out a field technician's kit and are quick to add.

Does my certification still count when I work in another state?

Yes, as long as you work for the employer that certified you; SNT-TC-1A certification is not tied to a state. It does not transfer to a new employer, which recertifies you from your records.

How do I become an NDT Level III?

Candidates usually pass the ASNT Basic and method examinations and are then certified by their employer. ASNT Level III training is self-paced preparation with Level III support.

Can I take AWS CWI exam prep in the region?

Yes. The six-day AWS CWI exam prep is offered as corporate training at your facility, online, or one-to-one online or in person, and AWS administers the examination and certifies. City pages cover Denver, Salt Lake City, Wichita, Tulsa and Oklahoma City.
